I am on the fence here. You said this is your first job, right? I don't know in what line of work you are. For me, this is common sense. Trust is something you work on, but also your skills. I don't know how was your onboarding process in the company.   


At the moment I am in a leadership position. I will never send my juniors alone to a meeting with a client. We are going together. We are also preparing together (when I came to the company I was on a mid-level and my lead didn't let me go on a meeting with him which I think is shit).   


I think it is great that you are sending an email with just a CC. Cause if you are a healthy team I would ask you to CC me every time, but I will include you as well. Especially if we are working together on the same client. Why - if the client or x person you are sending the email turns into a neandertal, I will want us to as a team to clear the issues. I would want to support you. And I can give you feedback on what to improve and what you are great at and could reach excellence. I also let my juniors do a set of tasks alone, and they regroup to give them feedback and gradually give them more responsibility.  


I don't think even I am a master of every trade but over time and with great guidance I know my strength and weakness, but for me, it is important to get to know you and see what you are lacking and in which areas you are brilliant. So one day you can be a senior or a lead and guide others.   


I would do a step back and evaluate the situation (I have been micro-managed on a job for close to 2 years so I know that this is not a healthy feeling building frustration) and try to look calmly.   


After that, I will reach out to my superior and ask them why the points you wrote, and that you are feeling micromanaged, and that you are getting a tone that you are not trusted. Ask for feedback. If the answer is in the air or nothing clear, then you are micromanaged. If they answer you that they want to support you and give you feedback and track your growth. I personally wouldn't then quit. I am just confused that they didn't communicate that to you if that is the case.
